title: How many Home Mortgage Loans may one customer hold at the same time?
content:
# How many Home Mortgage Loans may one customer hold at the same time?

This policy governs Home Mortgage Loans at the moment a new mortgage application is to be recorded. It sets the limits on how many mortgage loans one customer may hold, across all programs and within the requested program.

## Policy clauses

1. A customer may have several Home Mortgage Loans.
2. **Portfolio limit.** Before a new application is recorded, the count of the customer's mortgage loans in applied, active, delinquent or forbearance status must be below 4.
3. **Program limit.** The count of the customer's loans of the requested program, in those same statuses, must also be below that program's figure for the most loans of this program a customer may hold.
4. **FHA and VA.** Only one FHA or VA loan may be outstanding at a time for a primary residence.
5. **Loans that do not count.** Paid-off and withdrawn loans do not count.

## Evidence for the portfolio limit

- The count is taken from the bank's system records of the customer's mortgage loans and their statuses, not from the customer's own account of what they hold.
- The loans counted are those recorded under the same customer who is applying.
- The check is made before the new application is recorded.

## Checklist before a new application is recorded

| Check | Condition that must hold |
|---|---|
| Portfolio | Counted loans (applied, active, delinquent, forbearance) are fewer than 4 |
| Program | Counted loans of the requested program are fewer than that program's figure |
| FHA or VA for a primary residence | No second FHA or VA loan would be outstanding at the same time for a primary residence |

## Portfolio limit: boundary cases (hypothetical customers)

| Customer's loans on record | Counted loans | Below 4? |
|---|---|---|
| Two active, one delinquent | 3 | Yes |
| Two active, one in forbearance, one applied | 4 | No |
| Three active, one paid off, two withdrawn | 3 | Yes |
| Four paid off | 0 | Yes |

## Basis Q&A

- **Does a loan still in application count?** Yes. A loan in applied status is one of the four counted statuses.
- **Does a paid-off loan count toward either limit?** No. Paid-off and withdrawn loans do not count.
- **Hypothetical case.** A customer has one active FHA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage loan on a primary residence and asks to apply for a VA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage for a primary residence. Recording that application would put a second FHA or VA loan outstanding at the same time for a primary residence, which clause 4 does not allow.
- **Is the program limit a replacement for the portfolio limit?** No. Both must hold: a customer below the program's figure but already holding 4 counted loans does not meet the portfolio limit.
